info.desc: The album is a tragic rock opera about a doomed couple, and addresses themes of drug use and depression. Upon its release, the response of fans and critics was not positive as many were expecting another upbeat glam outing. Despite lukewarm reviews the album reached #7 in the UK album chart (Reed's best achievement there). Poor sales in the US (#98) and harsh criticism made Reed feel disillusioned about the album and in subsequent years he rarely played any Berlin material in his live shows. Over time many have come to consider Berlin to be among Lou Reed's best studio .

podcast.body: Lou Reed lacked strong instrumental knowledge for such a complex album and refused external help from other musicians or professional producers, which could have compensated for his deficiencies. While the album was "totally destroyed by critics" upon release, it has since been re-evaluated, with modern reviews from publications like Rolling Stone and Pitchfork being significantly more positive than their original scathing assessments. The album has gained "much context" and "charisma" within music culture over time. "Al final el disco acababa totalmente destrozado por la crítica."

podcast.body: The album exemplifies Lou Reed's unique method of storytelling in his songs, where each track functions like a "small novel" or a "small, self-contained, everyday story" presented with novelistic depth. "Berlin" specifically defines his lyrical approach, concentrating a concise, novel-like narrative into a three-minute song. "Y es que al final yo creo que en el álbum Berling de Lurry, tenemos esa manera de contar historias que tenían Lurry en sus canciones, que es casi como que cada canción de Lurry es como una pequeña novela o una pequeña historia cerrada, como muy cotidiana, pero contada como muy de novela."

podcast.body: This album was released just a few months after the "Transformer" tour concluded and was initially met with widespread critical condemnation, marking a "great fall" for Lou Reed. It was a highly complex conceptual album, narrating the harrowing story of a drug-addicted couple living through their miseries in New York City, blending song and narrative. The swift composition period (less than a year after "Transformer," including an 8-month tour) likely contributed to its initial failure, as it was the first time Lou Reed had to create 100% new material without relying on Velvet Underground leftovers. "Realmente Berling era un disco muy complejo porque era una especie de algún conceptual que venía como anarrar una historia, venía a contarnos la historia de una pareja de droga dictos que vivían toda su vida o un poco todas sus penurias por la ciudad de Nueva York."
